## The fix (item 2)
The root cause of "weekly/monthly caps aren't resumable" wasn't a futile resume — it was that the session got **dropped before its window could reset**. A paused Codex session stops writing to its rollout, so after `recent_secs` (6h) it fell out of the scan and `detect_codex` cleared it; a weekly reset is up to 7 days out, so the resume was lost.

Change in `remote_control/usage_limit/monitor.py` (`detect_codex`):
- A tracked-but-undiscovered session is now re-checked against the **full rollout history** (bounded by `gc_age_secs`). Still rate-limited → **keep it and refresh its reset target** so it resumes when the window refills; only clear on *positive* recovery (newest rollout healthy) or if it's gone.
- GC no longer evicts a session whose `reset_epoch` is still in the future.

This keeps the existing 5h-rolling behavior intact and adds **no skip/notify path** — it just maintains the resume whenever one is still makeable.

## Verification
- Full suite **185 green** (183 + 2 new regression tests: keep-quiet-long-cap, gc-keeps-future-reset — both fail against the old code).
